name: repository redirection is left in the environment
edits:
for var in REDIRECT_VARS:
        out.pop(var, None)
expect: git -C means what it says: GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR are removed

name: the throwaway index variable is stripped along with the redirections
expect: …GIT_INDEX_FILE is KEPT, because reviewed_state sets it on purpose

name: a null dirty map is collapsed into an empty one in the record
edits: "dirty": None if dirty is None else dict(dirty),
expect: a null dirty map survives into the record as null, not as an empty map

name: the prompt the run was dispatched with is dropped
expect: the verdict records the prompt the run was dispatched with

name: a deletion is skipped rather than recorded
edits:
if set(parts[3]) == {"0"}:
            continue
        dirty[path] = f"{parts[1]} {parts[3]}"
    return head.strip(), dirty
expect: …and a DELETED file is recorded as the all-zero entry, not skipped

name: the SOURCE mode is recorded instead of the destination mode
expect: …and the UNTRACKED one too, at its DESTINATION mode, not the 000000 source mode

name: the throwaway index is abandoned, so the repository's own index is used
expect: the repository's own index is untouched — the staging went to a throwaway one

name: every tracked file is recorded, changed or not
expect: a file identical to HEAD is not recorded as handed over

name: a wrapper with no head claims a clean tree instead of saying it could not look
expect: …and says it could not describe the tree with null, not with an empty map

name: the reason is dropped, so the classifier half stops reporting WHY a case failed
expect: the line keeps the canonical shape the harness documents

name: the contract is asserted against a stub instead of the harness's real parser
expect: the FAIL line this suite prints parses back to the case name, via the harness's OWN parser

name: the one FAIL-line shape reverts to got=, so every kill in this file goes unattributable
edits: return f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: got {got!r} want {want!r}{tail}"
return f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}: got={got!r}{tail}"
expect: the line keeps the canonical shape the harness documents: got=False

name: the collision refusal is dropped, so a DERIVED path overwrites committed testimony
expect: a DERIVED verdict path over a TRACKED file is refused

name: an unanswerable git query is read as answerable — the RULE's fail-open direction
expect: an UNANSWERABLE git query refuses rather than proceeding

name: path_is_tracked reports an INVALID git question as 'not tracked' — the FETCH's fail-open
expect: …and None for a path OUTSIDE that root — git's third answer, never read as False

name: the explicit --verdict escape is removed, so a deliberate replacement is refused too
expect: an EXPLICIT --verdict over a tracked file is ALLOWED — chosen, not derived

name: r4 H1: the allocator is dropped, so the documented mktemp call shape collides again
expect: H1: two DIFFERENT reviews at one HEAD cannot collide, even under the documented `--out "$(mktemp -d)/r.md"` shape that names them both `r`

name: r4 H1: the run token ignores the PROMPT, so two different reviews become one run
expect: the token separates two reviews by PROMPT at one head, at two distinct prompts

name: r4 H1: the run token ignores the HEAD, which is the r3 incident's own shape
expect: …and by HEAD at one prompt — the r3 incident, where an earlier session's verdict was lost

name: r4 M5: the refusal testifies to the very path it is protecting, destroying it
expect: the refusal's testimony is never the path it is protecting

name: r4 M2: a git that cannot be run is reported as a repository successfully built
expect: an ABSENT git binary is REPORTED, not raised — so the guard case below is reached rather than pre-empted by a traceback

name: r5: the run token ignores the TREE, so one brief over two trees is one run
expect: the same brief at the same commit over two DIFFERENT trees is two different runs

name: r5: 'could not describe the tree' collapses into 'the tree was clean'
edits: h.update(b"no-tree" if dirty is None else b"tree")
expect: …and 'the tree could not be described' is not the same answer as 'it was clean'

name: r5: the tree is hashed in dict order, so one tree can split into two runs
expect: the tree is order-insensitive, so two descriptions of one tree cannot split a run

name: r5: the run token narrows back to the 32-bit namespace a collision was found over
expect: …and by HEAD at one prompt — the r3 incident, where an earlier session's verdict was lost
